title: Sell Mineral Rights in Casper, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Casper, WY | Oil City Roots
metaDescription: Casper, WY built its identity on the Salt Creek oil field a century ago. Get a courthouse-grounded, honest read on your Natrona County mineral interest.
heroLead: Casper earned the nickname Oil City for a reason. Salt Creek, discovered north of town in the early 1900s, was one of the largest oil fields in the country at the time, and it built the refineries that shaped this city for a century.
intro: That history means Natrona County has a longer, deeper record of mineral ownership, leasing, and litigation than almost anywhere else in Wyoming. I've pulled deeds here that trace back through five or six owners over a hundred years, some tied to still-producing units, others to acreage that's sat quiet since the last boom.

If you're holding a Casper-area mineral interest, whether it's a family legacy piece or something you bought more recently, I want your actual documentation, deed, royalty statements, probate order, before I quote a single number, because this county has too much variation for guesswork.

sections.heading: Salt Creek's long production history
paragraphs: Salt Creek has produced for more than a century, moving through primary recovery, waterflood, and further enhanced-recovery phases as operators kept finding ways to extend the field's life. That longevity gives mineral owners inside the unit real documented royalty history to price against, something a lot of newer Wyoming plays simply don't have.
Decline on a field this mature tends to be gentle year over year rather than the steep early drop-off you'd see from a new horizontal well, which changes how I think about remaining value.

sections.heading: A century of refining and industry around the field
paragraphs: Casper's refineries and midstream infrastructure grew up around Salt Creek's output, and that industrial history shows up in local land records in ways that matter for title work, old right-of-way grants, easements, and multiple rounds of corporate mergers among the operators who've held leases here over the decades. Untangling which current entity actually holds an old lease is sometimes its own small research project.

sections.heading: Pricing a Casper-area interest
paragraphs: For producing interests, I lead with your trailing royalty statements and the unit's current enhanced-recovery status. For undeveloped acreage elsewhere in the county, I price against recent comparable Natrona County trades. Either way, I confirm your title through the county recorder before quoting anything.

faqs.question: Is Salt Creek still producing after all this time?
faqs.answer: Yes, portions continue under enhanced recovery. I'll check the current status specific to your interest.

faqs.question: My lease has changed hands between operators multiple times. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It affects who currently administers your royalty payments, but not your underlying ownership. I'll trace the current operator of record.

faqs.question: What if my interest is undeveloped, away from Salt Creek?
faqs.answer: I'll price it as speculative acreage based on comparable Natrona County trades, distinct from producing minerals.

faqs.question: How fast can a Casper-area sale close?
faqs.answer: Once title is confirmed, typically a few weeks, sometimes faster with clean, well-documented ownership.
